name: Chrome and Edge: no default fingerprint defense
plain: Chrome and Edge do not randomize or block fingerprinting APIs by default.
meaning: Chrome only reduced passive signals (User-Agent Reduction, Client Hints, partitioned storage). Privacy Budget never shipped, so canvas, WebGL, audio and fonts stay fully readable. Chrome has the largest fingerprinting surface.

web.api: Chrome settings (no toggle); Incognito changes nothing for fingerprints

steps: Site reads canvas, WebGL, fonts as usual
Chrome only coarsens UA string and some high entropy hints
Enterprise and extensions like CanvasBlocker can add noise

firefox.note: :Edge adds Strict tracking prevention but not fingerprint noise

limits.headline: Can't stop sites from using device traits to spot you in Chrome or Edge
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is how Chrome and Edge are set up by default
can: Let sites check canvas, graphics, audio and fonts as usual
Let sites see a trimmed down browser and system label
Keep cookies separate per site, which blocks some tracking
cannot: Add random noise to those checks
Block sites from fingerprinting by default
Hide your graphics card, fonts and sound setup
limits.differs: Safari, Firefox and Brave add protections that Chrome and Edge do not.

story.what_it_is: Chrome and Edge do not block or randomize most fingerprinting signals by default.

marketing.name: User agent reduction
marketing.pitch: Chrome says it is trimming detail from the browser's identity string to reduce passive tracking.

story.for_you: Most people use Chrome or Edge and leave the default settings on. That means canvas, audio and graphics details are available to most sites, with no warning to you.
story.for_makers: Fraud teams and ad tech rely on the open signals, because they work for the largest share of web users. Chrome has trimmed some data, like the version string, but still leaves most others readable.

use_cases.example: An ad network builds a device ID on Chrome visitors using canvas, fonts and graphics, because nothing stops it.
A bank trusts that Chrome reports honest values, and builds its device recognition on that.
A browser game reads graphics card names to pick the best quality setting for each player.
A visitor counting tool gets stable IDs from Chrome users and uses them for unique counts.
A big retailer detects bots by checking that Chrome's values look like a real laptop.
A streaming site reads device and codec details to choose video quality.
A developer uses the same signals to fix bugs that only appear on certain graphics cards.

technical_bounds: Incognito mode does not change fingerprints
Edge Strict mode blocks some trackers, not fingerprinting

value.abuse: Highest fingerprint fidelity of any browser

history.change: Reduced user agent string rolled out to all desktop and Android
Privacy Sandbox APIs largely wound down
